newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy President offers to tighten belt for Europe.
newsitem.headline: Italy President offers to tighten belt for Europe.

text.p: President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro has offered to tighten his belt for Europe by exposing his official income to the dread of all Italians -- income tax.
Scalfaro's offer was made in letters to Prime Minister Romano Prodi and other senior institutional figures which were made public by the presidential palace.
Newspapers splashed the story on Friday, reporting that the head of state's income would be halved as a result of the offer.

It was made as Italians prepare for a stringent 1997 budget, which will include a one-off "tax on Europe", to try to ensure the country meets the terms for membership of a planned single European currency.
The Italian president is paid an official tax-free salary of some 338 million lire ($220,000) a year, about 10 times the average gross income in Italy.
Scalfaro said he had tried in the past to have annual increases in his salary stopped but had had to accept them because the law on the issue had not been changed.
"This state of affairs absolutely must not go on. It must be remedied at a time when Italians are being asked to make significant sacrifices in order to reduce the public deficit," Scalfaro wrote.
